                    ### Question
                    A 3-year-old child referred for genetic consultation to assess psychomotor retardation, language delay and hyperactivity without significant dysmorphic features or associated malformations. He is the first child of a healthy, young and non-consanguineous couple. A maternal uncle has mental retardation and the maternal grandmother presented early ovarian failure. Which of the following diagnostic tests would be the most appropriate to establish the diagnosis?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Genetic study of triplet expansion of the FMR1 gene.
opb. Complete metabolic study.
opc. High resolution karyotype
opd. Psychometric evaluation

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Given the presentation of psychomotor retardation, language delay, and hyperactivity without dysmorphic features or malformations, the most appropriate diagnostic test would be a genetic study of triplet expansion of the FMR1 gene. This is supported by the family history of mental retardation and early ovarian failure, indicating a potential genetic etiology. The absence of dysmorphic features makes chromosomal abnormalities less likely, reducing the priority for high resolution karyotype. Complete metabolic study is of lower priority due to the low likelihood of an inherited metabolic disorder in this context.
